record.what_it_does: The Threads API lets developers create and publish posts, retrieve media and profiles, moderate replies, and access insights on a user's Threads account on their behalf.
record.auth_notes: Threads user access tokens conform to OAuth 2.0. Short-lived tokens (1 hour) are exchanged via an Authorization Window/Authorization Code flow, then exchanged for long-lived tokens (60 days) that can be refreshed. No API key or basic auth option exists; all access is per-user OAuth token scoped to specific permissions (threads_basic, threads_content_publish, threads_manage_replies, threads_read_replies, threads_manage_insights, threads_delete, threads_manage_mentions, threads_location_tagging).
record.access_notes: Self sign-up (create a Meta app, add Threads use case) is free, and app owners/added 'Threads testers' can immediately grant permissions and use the API. But for the app to work with arbitrary third-party Threads users (i.e., a real multi-user agent toolkit), each permission must be approved via Meta's App Review process and the app must be published/Live, and receiving full webhook data additionally requires Advanced Access and a verified business.
record.main_blocker: App Review / business verification required for production (non-tester) users
